# ConsoleWriter

A `TextWriter` over standard output that records the stream's failure where the caller can see it.

```rux
pub struct ConsoleWriter {
    // private fields
}
```

The protocol has one case for a destination failing, `WriterFailure`, and deliberately no room for the details:
Text has no vocabulary for a broken pipe and does not pretend to. So this adapter keeps both halves. It reports
`WriterFailure` to the formatter, which stops the write, and records the original [`IoError`](/docs/api/io/io-error) in the slot it was
built over, which is what the caller reads afterwards. Nothing about the stream failure is lost, and nothing
about it leaks into a package that could not interpret it. The slot starts as `none`, and holds the failure once
there is one.
The slot must outlive the writer. It is a stored address, so nothing here tracks that.

## Constructors

<h3 id="new"><code>ConsoleWriter</code></h3>

```rux
pub func ConsoleWriter(failure: *var IoError?) -> ConsoleWriter
```

A writer over standard output, recording into `failure`.
The slot is read before every write as well as written on failure, so a writer built over a slot that
already holds a failure writes nothing at all.

| Name      | Type            | Description                                                           |
| --------- | --------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `failure` | `*var IoError?` | where the first stream failure is recorded, `none` until there is one |

**Returns**: a writer over standard output

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Io/Src/TextBoundary.rux#L92)

## Implements TextWriter

`ConsoleWriter` conforms to `TextWriter`.

<h3 id="write"><code>Write</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Write(
    self: &var ConsoleWriter,
    bytes: char8[..]
) -> ! FormatError
```

Writes `bytes` to standard output.
Reports `WriterFailure` when the stream refuses, having recorded the original [`IoError`](/docs/api/io/io-error) in the slot. Once a
failure has been recorded every later write is refused without touching the stream, so a value that is
part-way through rendering does not go on writing into a handle that has already failed, and a trailing
newline is not emitted after a failed line. This is the only case this writer can produce: the bytes are not
revalidated, and standard output is not a bounded destination.

| Name    | Type        | Description            |
| ------- | ----------- | ---------------------- |
| `bytes` | `char8[..]` | the UTF-8 run to write |

**Returns**: success when the stream accepted the whole run

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Io/Src/TextBoundary.rux#L107)
